title: Optimization config change history UI (version timeline + filtering + status indicators)
creator: Kenji Nakamura
content:
Overview
We need a Console UI that makes Optimization Config changes traceable and safe to operate: a version timeline showing who/what/when, filtering by scope (tenant/model/region), and clear status indicators across lifecycle states (draft/validated/canary/promoted/active/rolled back/failed).

This ticket covers the information architecture and UI for the Change History view. Diff visualization and rollback confirmation UX are tracked separately (DES-212, DES-213).

Problem
Today operators and customer admins have no reliable, scannable history of optimization changes (batching/caching/quantization profiles). When regressions happen, on-call wastes time answering:
- “What changed?”
- “Who applied it, and to what scope?”
- “Did it fully roll out, or is it partial?”
- “What’s active right now?”

Goals
1) Provide a single place in Console to answer: who changed what, when, and where it applied.
2) Make rollout state legible: canary vs promoted vs paused vs failed vs rolled back.
3) Enable quick narrowing by scope (tenant/model/region) without hunting across pages.
4) Ensure history is useful in incidents (fast scan, links to metrics and rollback).

Non-goals
- Designing the diff algorithm or field-level risk scoring (covered in DES-212; API in ENG-4822).
- Designing the rollback confirmation modal content (DES-213).
- Fully automated rollback flows and hands-off remediation.

Primary users
- Internal on-call / SRE: needs fast incident context and the ability to validate whether a rollback “took.”
- Customer admins (Hosted/Dedicated) with permissions: needs visibility into changes and audit trail.
- Private operators: same mental model; UI parity depends on deployment (Private may use pinned versions + export). This UI should still represent the control-plane history model.

Key objects (mental model)
- Optimization Config Version: immutable version record with metadata (author, created time, validation status, notes).
- Apply/Rollout event: an action that attempts to make a version active for a scope. Rollouts can be staged and can fail/rollback.
- Active pointer: for a scope, which version is currently active.

Information architecture (Console)
Left nav: Optimize → Optimization Configs
- Configs list (existing)
- Config details page
  - Tabs: Overview | History | Diff (link) | Rollouts (optional; can be folded into History)

We will implement History as the default landing section within a config’s details page for faster discoverability.

History view: layout + components
A) Header
- Breadcrumb: Optimize / Optimization Configs / {Config Name}
- Title: {Config Name}
- Right-side: “Create new version” (if permission) + “Apply version” (if permission)
- Secondary: “Active version: v{N}” pill; hover shows exact scope if filtered

B) Scope filter row (sticky)
Filters are intended to reduce noise first, then show the timeline.
- Tenant (required in internal tooling; for customer console the tenant is implicit)
- Model (dropdown; supports “All models”) 
- Region (dropdown; supports “All regions”)
- Deployment mode: Hosted | Dedicated | Private (if visible in Console context)
- Time range: last 24h / 7d / 30d / custom
- Status: All | Active | Promoted | Canary | Paused | Failed | Rolled back

Filtering behavior
- Filters apply to the timeline items and also to the “Active version” pill.
- When filters represent a scope broader than a rollout event (e.g., “All regions”), we still show events but annotate that the rollout occurred on a subset.

C) Timeline list
A reverse-chronological timeline of events grouped by Version, with latest activity first.

Row anatomy (each timeline card)
- Left: status icon + status label (see Status taxonomy below)
- Main title: “v{N} {version_name or short summary}”
- Subheader: “Applied to {scope summary}” (e.g., “tenant: acme • model: llama-3.1-70b • region: us-east-1”) 
- Metadata line: “Triggered by {actor} • {timestamp} • {source: Console/API}”
- Optional chips:
  - “Canary 5% → 25%” or “Paused at 10%”
  - “Gates: latency ✅ • 5xx ✅ • evals ✅/—” (read-only; click opens details drawer)
  - “Rollback target: v{M}” if this is a rollback event
- Right: actions
  - “View diff” (links to Diff tab pre-selected to v{N} vs prior active)
  - “Rollback” (if allowed, version is not currently active, and a rollback is valid)

Expandable details drawer (per card)
- Full scope JSON-ish summary (human-readable, not raw)
- Rollout stages + timestamps: validated → canary started → promoted → completed
- Gate evaluation snapshots (links out to dashboards)
- Audit correlation: request_id / change_id
- Link: “Open in Audit Log” (if the org has access) / “Copy event ID”

D) Empty / loading / error states
- Empty history: show explanatory text + CTA “Create a version” (if permission). For customers without permission: “No changes recorded for this scope/time range.”
- Loading: skeleton cards with the timeline structure.
- Error: “Unable to load history” + retry; show last successful refresh timestamp if available.

Status taxonomy + indicators (final)
We need consistent, unambiguous states that map to the backend lifecycle and support incident scanning.

Version-centric states (applies to version records)
- Draft (gray): created but not validated
- Validated (blue): passes schema + semantic validation

Rollout-centric states (applies to apply/promotion/rollback attempts)
- Canary in progress (purple): rollout started and is progressing
- Paused (yellow): rollout paused by operator or automation, awaiting action
- Promoted (blue): promoted to broader scope but not yet completed
- Active (green): currently active for the selected scope
- Completed (green): rollout finished successfully (may be active or replaced later)
- Failed (red): rollout failed gates or apply transaction
- Rolled back (orange): rollback executed (shows target version)

Important nuance: “Active” is scope-relative
A version can be Active for one region and not for another. The UI will:
- Only show “Active” in context of a specific scope (i.e., when tenant+model+region is specified).
- When scope is broad (All regions/models), show “Active in {X}/{Y} regions” instead of a single Active badge.

Partial rollout representation
When a rollout is staged, display:
- Progress bar: “Applied to 10% of traffic” OR “2/10 shards”
- “Mixed state” pill when the filter includes multiple scopes with different actives
- CTA: “View rollout details” opens drawer with per-region/shard breakdown (text list; future enhancement to a table)

Data requirements (for ENG)
From history endpoint (ENG-4828 / PR-19960):
Required fields per timeline item:
- version_id, version_number, version_name (optional), created_at
- actor: name, type (human/service), source (Console/API)
- event_type: create | validate | apply_start | apply_pause | apply_resume | promote | apply_complete | rollback | apply_fail
- status: derived display state
- scope: tenant_id, model_id, region, deployment_mode; plus “scope_summary” string preferred
- rollout metadata: canary_percent, stage, shard_count, completed_shards
- gate summary: error_rate_gate (pass/fail/unknown), latency_gate, eval_gate
- correlation: request_id, change_id/audit_event_id
Pagination:
- Timeline should be pageable; default 50 items; preserve filters in URL.

Copy + terminology
- Prefer “Version” and “Change” over “Config update” (more concrete for operators).
- Use “Rolled back to v{M}” (verb) rather than “Reverted.”
- Use “Applied” for initial action; “Promoted” for expanding scope; “Active” for current state.

Accessibility and scanability
- Do not rely solely on color for status; include icon + text.
- Timestamps in relative form (e.g., “14 min ago”) with hover absolute.
- Keyboard navigation: timeline cards focusable; drawer operable via keyboard.

Edge cases to cover
- Version deleted? (Should not happen; versions are immutable. If a record is missing, show “Unknown version” and keep event.)
- Actor unknown (service account): show “System” + service name if available.
- Rollback executed while apply was in progress: show two events with a “Conflict resolved” note if backend provides; otherwise show chronological events and rely on status.
- RBAC: If user lacks rollback permission, hide action but still show event history.

Deliverables
- Figma: Optimization Config → History tab designs (desktop)
- Component specs: timeline card variants + status icons
- Interaction notes: filtering, mixed-state, drawer behavior

Links
- PRD: confluence/product-docs/requirements/safe-apply-rollback-prd.json
- Design spec (eng): confluence/product-docs/design-specs/optimization-config-versioning-design.json
- Related design tickets: DES-212 (diff view), DES-213 (confirmation modal)
- Engineering dependencies: ENG-4828 (Console history/rollback), ENG-4821 (schema)

Decision log
2025-09-26: Agreed with Chloe Martin (Console EM) to make History the default tab on Config Details page, not a separate page. Rationale: on-call enters via a config link and needs context immediately.
2025-10-02: Confirmed with Sean Gallagher (SRE) that partial rollout must be visible in the list view without extra clicks. Added progress bar + mixed-state pill.
2025-10-07: Confirmed with Marcus Lin (Security) that audit correlation fields should be visible but not overwhelming; placed behind expandable drawer with “Copy event ID.”

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should we show raw JSON diff in history? A: No; history shows summary + links to Diff tab (DES-212).
- Q: What is the minimum scope for “Active” badge? A: tenant+model+region required; otherwise show aggregated active coverage.

QA / acceptance criteria
- Timeline shows who/what/when for each event.
- Filtering by tenant/model/region/status/time works and is URL-addressable.
- Status indicators match taxonomy above and do not depend solely on color.
- Partial rollout can be identified from the list view.
- Each event has a path to: diff, rollout details, and audit correlation (if available).

Final notes for implementation
- Recommend a shared “StatusBadge” component used across History, Diff header, and Rollout widgets.
- Strongly recommend rendering scope summary strings server-side to avoid client inconsistencies (model naming, region formatting).

Updates
- 2025-10-14: Design signed off by Marissa Cole (Product) and Chloe Martin (Console EM). Hand-off complete; implementation proceeds under ENG-4828.
